findings.title: SkillGen paper's same-seed statement is not implementation-verified as model-inference RNG on ScienceWorld
findings.observation: Appendix C.2 of arXiv:2605.10999v1 states that each held-out instance is rolled out once without and once with the skill using the same instance identifier and random seed, default seed 42; Appendix C.3 also calls decoding deterministic at temperature 0. In the observed public ScienceWorld implementation, however, ScienceWorld is reduced to an offline plan-generation benchmark over fixed gold-path-derived prompts and does not run the ScienceWorld environment/JVM. The public eval path uses random.Random(args.seed) to select the instance subset, while the OpenRouter chat path exposes model/messages/temperature/max_tokens and no inference seed. Thus current public code does not bind the paper's same-seed statement to model-inference RNG equivalence.
findings.scope_guard: Do not infer that the paper is wrong or that temperature-zero API decoding is necessarily stochastic. Safe conclusion: inference-RNG equivalence is not executable-provenance-bound by the inspected public source; either paper-time runs used additional controls not preserved here or same seed refers to sampling/dataset protocol.

findings.title: The seed-provenance gap is already present in an observed preprint-adjacent public source snapshot
findings.observation: The Git history query for llm.py exposes commit f7304a5595ca35d92500f1be2cceb4aca545fe0b with Git author/committer timestamp 2026-05-08T17:32:39Z, while arXiv v1 is dated 2026-05-09. At that exact commit, llm.py already routes chat through OpenRouter with model/messages/temperature/max_tokens and no exposed inference seed; eval_skill.py already samples instances with random.Random(args.seed); scienceworld_adapter.py already defines the no-live-environment offline plan variant; prepare_scienceworld.py already uses seed 42 for deterministic stratified dataset construction; artifacts.py already serializes inference_model/judge_model without provider execution revision or inference RNG binding.
findings.scope_guard: Git author/committer time is chronology metadata only, not a server-attested public-release time or evaluated-run execution certificate. This source snapshot is preprint-adjacent evidence, not a proven paper-run source revision.

findings.title: ScienceWorld seed 42 is concretely embedded in static dataset construction
findings.observation: At the same historical source snapshot, prepare_scienceworld.py documents the 150-train/100-test pilot with --seed 42 and uses random.Random(seed) for stratified sampling, with the test pool using seed XOR 0xDEAD. The versioned historical data/scienceworld/test.json identifies itself as scienceworld_test_n100_seed42 and contains fixed offline-plan prompts plus gold-path metadata. This provides direct executable evidence for a dataset-construction meaning of seed 42 in ScienceWorld, independent of any unobserved model-provider randomness semantics.
findings.scope_guard: This does not prove that the paper's phrase 'same random seed' referred only to dataset construction; it shows that this meaning is explicitly implemented while an inference seed is not exposed in the inspected source.

findings.title: Broader indexed SkillGen artifact search still yields code/paper metadata rather than static ScienceWorld paired-run bytes
findings.observation: Targeted indexed searches for ScienceWorld effectiveness baseline/with-skill JSONL, skill.json, Zenodo/OSF/dataset records, and Hugging Face datasets surfaced the official code repository and paper-index pages but no static ScienceWorld effectiveness run bundle. The official README itself confirms the bundled dataset splits are the experiment splits and points live evaluation to generated local skill_output paths rather than a checked-in result archive.
findings.scope_guard: Negative evidence is limited to the exact indexed searches and official surfaces checked in this run; it is not a global proof of absence.
